projects.title: The Haussmann Pavilion
projects.subtitle: Reimagining classic 19th-century proportions for serene contemporary living
projects.concept: A contemplative dialogue between historical heritage and radical architectural minimalism. The design strips back layers of decorative additions to celebrate the soaring 4.2-meter ceiling heights, monumental crown mouldings, and restored chevron oak parquet, contrasted by monolithic travertine blocks and unlacquered burnished bronze.
projects.clientBrief: The clients, an art collector and a private equity director, sought a home that serves as both a tranquil sanctuary from urban intensity and a curated gallery for their collection of Post-War abstract canvases and Brutalist ceramics.
projects.challengeSolution: The primary challenge lay in re-organizing a fragmented 1890 floor plan without altering the listed perimeter walls. We introduced a central sculptural monolith in fluted travertine that discretely conceals a guest suite, wine cellar, and state-of-the-art climate control, while guiding natural light through double-height steel-framed glass portals.
projects.testimonialQuote: Atelier Élysée transformed an overwhelming historical apartment into a breathable, meditative composition of light and stone. Every morning here feels like an unhurried reverie.

projects.title: Montecito Coastal Retreat
projects.subtitle: Warm modernist villa grounded in earthen textures and ocean light
projects.concept: Grounded in the terrain of the Santa Ynez foothills, this residence celebrates natural continuity between interior and landscape. Broad spans of floor-to-ceiling pocketing glazing dissolve boundaries, framed by hand-rammed earth walls, bleached white oak millwork, and monolithic basalt counters.
projects.clientBrief: Create an effortlessly luxurious family home that withstands coastal elements while exuding timeless quietude and warmth.
projects.challengeSolution: By lowering the formal living room into a sun-dappled sunken conversation lounge surrounded by textured earthen walls, we created an intimate anchor point inside an expansive 600-square-meter floor plan.
projects.testimonialQuote: The house feels alive with the changing light. The team understood our family rhythm completely—creating something monumental yet profoundly comfortable.

projects.title: Lumière Design Studio & Gallery
projects.subtitle: Architectural cast-iron loft converted into a creative sanctuary and flagship atelier
projects.concept: Transforming an authentic 1888 industrial cast-iron warehouse into a tactile spatial experience. Raw structural brickwork is softened with warm lime-wash glazes, blackened steel partitions, acoustic felt ceiling vaults, and custom oak library tables.
projects.clientBrief: Design a multifunctional headquarters for a high-end luxury fashion brand, balancing collaborative studio environments with private client fitting salons and an exhibition gallery.
projects.challengeSolution: We engineered custom mobile monolithic joinery units on concealed industrial tracks, allowing the main gallery floor to effortlessly transition from an open 100-seat runway presentation into intimate private design pods within minutes.
projects.testimonialQuote: The response from our global clientele has been overwhelming. The studio captures our brand ethos: timeless craftsmanship, uncompromising material honesty.

projects.title: Palazzo Bellini Restoration
projects.subtitle: Preserving 17th-century Baroque frescoes within a contemporary private residence
projects.concept: An exacting archival preservation merged with understated contemporary Italian joinery. Damaged gilded stuccos were stabilized by master conservators, framed by bespoke floor planes in terracotta pastellone and clean walnut millwork that floats clear of historic surfaces.
projects.clientBrief: A heritage preservation project requiring rigorous academic accuracy alongside 21st-century thermal comfort, acoustic seclusion, and luxury amenities.
projects.challengeSolution: To prevent trenching into fragile historic stonework, all mechanical, electrical, and geothermal HVAC lines were routed through bespoke raised floating baseboards crafted from matching walnut and brushed brass.
projects.testimonialQuote: Working with Éléonore and her studio was a revelation. They did not just design our home; they resurrected centuries of Mediterranean heritage with peerless sensitivity.

projects.title: Le Belvédère Alpine Chalet
projects.subtitle: Monolithic granite and charred larch amidst the Mont Blanc range
projects.concept: A contemporary take on traditional Savoyard architecture. Massive fireplaces chiselled from local Mont Blanc granite anchor wide open entertaining salons clad in hand-planed larch and Belgian wools.
projects.clientBrief: Create a private 8-suite ski lodge with spa, indoor vitality pool, and private tasting cellar that redefines alpine luxury without rustic clichés.
projects.challengeSolution: We incorporated an underground glass-encased wine cellar carved directly into the mountain bedrock, framed by indirect warm wash lighting that accentuates natural stone stratifications.

projects.title: The Kyoto Garden Residence
projects.subtitle: Meditative spatial sequencing, Hinoki woodcraft, and interior courtyard views
projects.concept: Designed according to classical Shakkei (borrowed scenery) principles, the residence opens entirely to a moss and bamboo courtyard, incorporating hand-woven rush tatami mats, cedar joinery, and handmade Echizen washi screens.
projects.clientBrief: A dual-nationality family home balancing traditional Japanese rituals with contemporary entertaining standards.
projects.challengeSolution: We devised concealed sliding shoji partitions that slide into hollow wall cavities, allowing the entire living space to expand into an unbroken 30-meter pavilion connecting three secluded courtyard gardens.

articles.title: The Quiet Luxury of Tactility: Living with Raw Travertine and French Oak
articles.excerpt: In an era dominated by smooth glass screens and uniform synthetic surfaces, the true luxury of a home resides in materials that speak back through texture, weight, and honest imperfection.

content.text: When we walk barefoot across a honed silver travertine floor on a cool morning, or run our fingertips over the fibrous grain of unlacquered quarter-sawn French oak, something subtle yet profound shifts in our physiological state. We are grounded in the physical reality of the earth.
The Honesty of Porosity

Travertine is geological memory captured in stone. Formed by rapid precipitation of calcium carbonate at hot springs and geothermal geysers, its natural cavities and sediment striations are not defects to be filled with opaque epoxy; they are the rhythmic signature of mineral history. In our projects, we celebrate these open veins, opting for brushed or honed satin finishes rather than reflective high polishes.
A home should not be an antiseptic museum of untouched perfection, but an organic landscape that receives the patina of daily life with grace.

Similarly, French oak possesses a biological warmth that synthetic laminates can never emulate. The tannins within genuine oak react over decades to sunlight and humidity, developing a silver-grey or honey-toned sheen that deepens with every season.
Designing for the Senses Beyond the Eye

Too often, contemporary interior design is conceived exclusively for two-dimensional photography—a visual spectacle designed to capture fleeting attention on social feeds. At Atelier Élysée, we prioritize acoustics, temperature, scent, and hand-feel. When a room sounds serene because natural lime-wash plaster absorbs harsh acoustic reflections, the luxury is unmistakable.

articles.title: Restraint as an Art: Why the Most Luxurious Spaces Whisper Rather Than Shout
articles.excerpt: True sophistication does not scream for validation. It reveals itself in proportional harmony, shadow, and the courage to leave walls unencumbered.

content.text: There is a common misconception that luxury equates to abundance—more mouldings, more gold leaf, more intricate joinery, more layers. Yet historically, the most celebrated architectural masterworks, from Japanese tea pavilions to Cistercian monasteries, have derived their emotional resonance from radical reduction.
The Power of Negative Space

Negative space is not empty space; it is spatial breath. An unadorned plaster wall washed by afternoon daylight allows a single sculptural olive tree or a patinated bronze bowl to possess genuine gravitas. When every surface is screaming for attention, nothing is heard.
Simplicity is not the starting point. It is the hard-won culmination of removing everything that does not contribute to harmony.

When we strip away extraneous ornamentation, our attention naturally fixes on the caliber of execution. An unadorned doorway demands that the reveal line be flawless; a monolithic stone island requires that the mitred corners align to within a tenth of a millimeter. Restraint is the ultimate test of craftsmanship.

articles.title: The Haussmannian Dialogue: Marrying 19th-Century Plasterwork with Minimalist Modernity
articles.excerpt: A practical and philosophical guide to renovating historic European apartments without erasing their soul or succumbing to museum-like stagnation.

content.text: Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann redefined Paris between 1853 and 1870, creating an urban typology characterized by ashlar stone facades, continuous wrought-iron balconies, and interiors adorned with intricate plaster rosettes and chevron parquet. Today, living in these spaces requires a thoughtful balance between preservation and contemporary functionality.
The Non-Interference Principle

When intervening in a listed historic apartment, our philosophy is rooted in reversibility and visual autonomy. Rather than mimicking historical mouldings in new partition walls, we clearly differentiate new contemporary interventions through modern material expressions: blackened steel, monolithic unpolished marble, and floating walnut joinery.
History becomes vibrant not when we freeze it in amber, but when we invite it into dialogue with contemporary life.

By keeping modern cabinetry floating slightly above the floor and terminating millwork below the original ceiling cornices, the historic volume remains legible in its entirety. The dialogue between the 19th and 21st centuries becomes an active source of daily pleasure.

articles.title: Light as Matter: Sculpting Volumetric Shadows in Modern Residential Architecture
articles.excerpt: Architectural lighting should not simply illuminate darkness; it should reveal form, sculpt volume, and create an emotional rhythm across the day.

content.text: In his timeless essay In Praise of Shadows, Jun’ichirō Tanizaki writes that beauty does not exist in the object itself, but in the patterns of shadows, the light and the darkness, that one object creates against another. Modern architecture too frequently relies on aggressive, glaring ceiling spotlights that obliterate nuance.
The Three-Tier Illumination Strategy

We approach illumination in three distinct architectural layers: Low-level perimeter graze, mid-level focal warmth, and soft ambient reflection. By washing an earthen plaster wall with low-angle warm light (2400K–2700K), we emphasize the subtle undulations of the hand-troweled surface while keeping glare entirely out of the line of sight.

articles.title: Curating an Heirloom Palette: Timeless Earth Tones for 2026 and Beyond
articles.excerpt: Moving past ephemeral color trends toward grounded earth pigments: raw umber, warm chalk, limestone, burnt sienna, and oxidized bronze.

content.text: Interior design is frequently assaulted by seasonal ‘colors of the year’ engineered to generate obsolescence. But when you are selecting materials for a residence meant to stand for decades, trend-following is an act of aesthetic bankruptcy.

Our studio anchors all material palettes in the natural geological spectrum: Warm Ivory (#F7F5F0), Soft Linen Beige (#E9E3D9), Deep Charcoal (#242321), and Earthy Raw Ochre (#A58A70). These shades reflect natural sunlight without distortion and welcome changing seasonal light effortlessly.
